sonnet.problem: The fill-in-the-blank asks the baker to guess the wording of the verse ("wrapped in a ___"). Nothing on the earlier card lets them reason out "cloud". The other options, robe and sash, are equally plausible.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to complete the line with "thunders". The baker has never seen that word, and the story card before it only says "other voices sound". The question tests the verse's wording, not reasoned meaning.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The true/false statement repeats the right answer from the previous card ("the mystery of God will be fulfilled") and builds its claim on it. That answer was already shown on card 14.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the verb in the angel's command ("take it and ___ it"). The story card before it gives nothing to reason from. The baker can only guess "eat" from the verse's wording.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
